source.title: Open Problems in Analysis of Boolean Functions

accepted.question_text: Find an explicit Boolean function f:{0,1}^n→{0,1} in NP such that for every polynomial p:{0,1}^n→{0,1} over F_2 of degree at most log_2 n, the correlation |E[(-1)^(f(x)+p(x))]| is at most 1/n.
accepted.context_brief: Correlation bounds for low-degree F_2 polynomials

evidence.quote: Statement: Find an explicit (i.e., in NP) function f : /BY n 2 → /BY 2 such that we have the correlation bound | E[(− 1)〈f (x),p(x)〉]| ≤ 1/n for every /BY 2-polynomial p : /BY n 2 → /BY 2 of degree at most log 2 n.

accepted.question_text: Let a∈R^n satisfy ||a||_2=1. Is it always true that for uniformly random x∈{-1,1}^n, the probability that |⟨a,x⟩|≤1 is at least 1/2?

evidence.quote: Statement: Let a ∈ /CA n have ∥a∥2 = 1. Then Prx∼ {− 1,1}n[|〈 a, x〉| ≤ 1] ≥ 1/2.

accepted.question_text: Let f:{-1,1}^n→R_{≥0} satisfy E[f]=1, and fix 0<ρ<1. Must the tail of the noise operator obey Pr[T_ρ f ≥ t] = o(1/t) as t→∞?

evidence.quote: Statement: Let f : {− 1, 1}n → /CA ≥ 0 have E[ f ] = 1. Fix any 0 < ρ < 1. Then Pr[Tρ f ≥ t] < o(1/t).

accepted.question_text: For every Boolean function f:{-1,1}^n→{-1,1}, is the polynomial degree deg(f) bounded by a polynomial in the maximum sensitivity sens[f]=max_x |{i∈[n]: f(x) ≠ f(x⊕i)}|?

evidence.quote: Statement: For any f : {− 1, 1}n → {− 1, 1} it holds that deg( f ) ≤ poly(sens[ f ]), where sens[ f ] is the (maximum) sensitivity , max x | {i ∈ [n] : f (x) ̸= f (x⊕ i)}| .

accepted.question_text: Among all degree-k polynomial threshold functions f:{-1,1}^n→{-1,1}, is the maximum total influence attained by the symmetric threshold function of the form f(x)=sgn(p(x_1+⋯+x_n)), where p is a degree-k univariate polynomial alternating sign on the k+1 values of x_1+⋯+x_n closest to 0?

evidence.quote: Statement: Among degree- k polynomial threshold functions f : {− 1, 1}n → {− 1, 1}, the one with maximal total inﬂuence is the symmetric one f (x) = sgn(p(x1 + · · · +xn)), where p is a degree- k univariate polynomial which al- ternates sign on the k + 1 values of x1 + · · · +xn closest to 0.

accepted.question_text: Suppose A is a nonempty subset of F_2^n with doubling |A+A|≤C|A|. Must A be coverable by poly(C) affine subspaces, each having cardinality at most |A|?

evidence.quote: Statement: Suppose /⌉mptys⌉tstr⌉ss ̸=A ⊆ /BY n 2 satisﬁes | A + A| ≤ C| A| . Then A can be cov- ered by the union of poly( C) afﬁne subspaces, each of cardinality at most | A| .

accepted.question_text: Let f:{-1,1}^n→{-1,1} be computable by a DNF of size s>1, and let ε∈(0,1/2]. Is the Fourier spectrum of f always ε-concentrated on some set F of Fourier coefficients with |F|≤s^{O(log(1/ε))}?

evidence.quote: Statement: Let f : {− 1, 1}n → {− 1, 1} be computable by a DNF of size s > 1 and let ǫ∈ (0, 1/2]. Then f ’s Fourier spectrum is ǫ-concentrated on a collection F with | F | ≤ sO(log(1/ǫ)).

accepted.question_text: Given a finite set T of vectors in R^n, define b(T)=E_{x∼{-1,1}^n}[max_{t∈T}⟨t,x⟩] and let g(T) be the analogous quantity for standard Gaussian x. Does there always exist a finite set T′ such that g(T′)≤O(b(T)) and every t∈T is within ℓ_1-distance O(b(T)) of some t′∈T′?

evidence.quote: Statement: Let T be a ﬁnite collection of vectors in /CA n. Deﬁne b(T) = Ex∼ {− 1,1}n[maxt∈ T 〈t, x〉], and deﬁne g(T) to be the same quantity except with x ∼ /CA n Gaussian. Then there exists a ﬁnite collection of vectors T′ such that g(T′) ≤ O(b(T)) and ∀ t ∈ T ∃t′∈ T′ ∥t − t′∥1 ≤ O(b(T)).

accepted.question_text: Is there a universal constant C such that every Boolean function f:{-1,1}^n→{-1,1} satisfies H[\hat f^2] ≤ C·I[f], where H[\hat f^2]=∑_S \hat f(S)^2 log_2(1/\hat f(S)^2) is the spectral entropy and I[f] is the total influence?

evidence.quote: Statement: There is a universal constant C such that for any f : {− 1, 1}n → {− 1, 1} it holds that H[ ˆf 2] ≤ C ·I[ f ], where H[ ˆf 2] = ∑ S ˆf (S)2 log2 1 / ˆf (S)2 is the spectral entropy and I[ f ] is the total inﬂuence.

accepted.question_text: Let f:{-1,1}^n→{-1,1} be a linear threshold function with n odd. Is it true that for every ρ∈[0,1], the noise stability satisfies Stab_ρ[f] ≥ Stab_ρ[Maj_n]?
accepted.context_brief: Noise stability of majority among LTFs

evidence.quote: Statement: Let f : {− 1, 1}n → {− 1, 1} be a linear threshold function, n odd. Then for all ρ ∈ [0, 1], Stabρ[ f ] ≥ Stabρ[Majn].

accepted.question_text: Fix r≥6, odd n, and 0<ε<1/2. For f:{-1,1}^n→{-1,1}, let P(f)=Pr[f(y^(1))=f(y^(2))=⋯=f(y^(r))], where x is uniform on {-1,1}^n and each y^(i) is an independent ε-noisy copy of x. Among odd Boolean functions, is P(f) maximized by some majority function Maj_k on an odd number k of inputs?

evidence.quote: Statement: Fix r ∈ /C6 , n odd, and 0 < ǫ< 1/2. For f : {− 1, 1}n → {− 1, 1}, deﬁne P( f ) = Pr[ f (y(1)) = f (y(2)) = · · ·f (y(r))], where x ∼ {− 1, 1}n is chosen uniformly and then each y(i) is (independently) an ǫ-noisy copy of x. Is it true that P( f ) is maximized among odd functions f by the Majority function Maj k on some odd number of inputs k?

accepted.question_text: If f:{-1,1}^n→{-1,1} is the intersection of k linear threshold functions, must its noise sensitivity satisfy NS_δ[f] ≤ O(√(log k))·√δ?
accepted.context_brief: Noise sensitivity of intersections of halfspaces

evidence.quote: Statement: Let f : {− 1, 1}n → {− 1, 1} be the intersection (AND) of k linear threshold functions. Then NSδ[ f ] ≤ O( √ log k) · /ra⌈〉callow δ.

accepted.question_text: Let f:{-1,1}^n→{-1,1} be unbiased. Draw z∈{-1,0,1}^n by keeping each coordinate as ±1 with probability p/2 each and replacing it by 0 with probability 1-p, independently across coordinates. When p<1/2 and n is odd, is E_z[|f(z)|] maximized by the majority function, interpreting f through its multilinear expansion?

evidence.quote: Statement: Let f : {− 1, 1}n → {− 1, 1} be an unbiased function. Let z ∼ {− 1, 0, 1}n be a “random restriction” in which each coordinate zi is (indepen- dently) ± 1 with probability p/2 each, and 0 with probability 1 − p. Assuming p < 1/2 and n odd, is it true that Ez[| f (z)| ] is maximized when f is the ma- jority function? (Here we identify f with its multilinear expansion.)

accepted.question_text: Let A⊆F_2^n. Suppose one must remove ε·2^n elements from A to make it triangle-free, meaning there are no x,y with x,y,x+y all in A. Must the triangle density Pr[x,y,x+y∈A] be at least poly(ε) for independent uniform x,y∈F_2^n?

evidence.quote: Statement: Let A ⊆ /BY n 2 . Suppose that ǫ2n elements must be removed from A in order to make it “triangle-free” (meaning there does not e xist x, y, x + y ∈ A). Is it true that Prx,y[x, y, x + y ∈ A] ≥ poly(ǫ), where x and y are independent and uniform on /BY n 2 ?

accepted.question_text: Fix a constant α>0 and let A⊆F_2^n have density at least α. Does the sumset A+A necessarily contain a subspace of codimension O(√n)?

evidence.quote: Statement: Fix a constant α > 0. Let A ⊆ /BY n 2 have density at least α. Is it true that A + A contains a subspace of codimension O(/ra⌈〉callown)?

accepted.question_text: Let f:{-1,1}^n→[-1,1] have polynomial degree at most k. Must there exist a coordinate i∈[n] whose influence satisfies Inf_i[f] ≥ (Var[f]/k)^{O(1)}?
accepted.context_brief: Influence lower bounds for bounded low-degree functions

evidence.quote: Statement: Let f : {− 1, 1}n → [− 1, 1] have degree at most k. Then there exists i ∈ [n] with Infi[ f ] ≥ (Var[ f ]/k)O(1).

accepted.question_text: Fix a collection of forbidden affine patterns {(M_1,σ_1),(M_2,σ_2),…}, where M_i is a matrix over F_2 and σ_i is a binary pattern, and let P_n be the property that f:F_2^n→{0,1} is (M_i,σ_i)-free for every i. Does P_n always admit a one-sided-error constant-query property-testing algorithm?

evidence.quote: Statement: Let M ∈ /BY m× k 2 and σ ∈ {0, 1}k. Say that f : /BY n 2 → {0, 1} is ( M, σ)- free if there does not exist X = (x(1), . . .,x(k)) ... Now ﬁx a (possi- bly inﬁnite) collection {(M1, σ1), (M2, σ2), · · ·} and consider the property P n of functions f : /BY n 2 → {0, 1} that f is ( M i, σ i)-free for all i. Then there is a one-sided error , constant-query property-testing algorithm for P n.

accepted.question_text: Fix 0≤ρ,μ,ν≤1. If A,B⊆R^n have Gaussian measures μ and ν and A is centrally symmetric (A=-A), what is the minimum possible value of Pr[x∈A, y∈B] when (x,y) is a pair of ρ-correlated n-dimensional Gaussian vectors?

evidence.quote: Statement: Fix 0 ≤ ρ, µ , ν ≤ 1. Suppose A, B ⊆ /CA n have Gaussian measure µ , ν respectively . Further , supposeA is centrally symmetric: A = − A. What is the minimal possible value of Pr[x ∈ A, y ∈ B], when ( x, y) are ρ-correlated n-dimensional Gaussians?

accepted.question_text: Fix 0≤ρ≤1. Among all partitions of R^n into q parts of equal Gaussian measure, with 3≤q≤n+1, is the maximum noise stability achieved by a standard simplex partition? Likewise, for −1≤ρ≤0, does the standard simplex partition minimize the noise stability?

evidence.quote: Statement: Fix 0 ≤ ρ ≤ 1. Then among all partitions of /CA n into 3 ≤ q ≤ n + 1 parts of equal Gaussian measure, the maximal noise stabilit y at ρ occurs for a “standard simplex partition”. ... Further , for − 1 ≤ ρ ≤ 0 the standard simplex partition minimizes noise stability at ρ.

accepted.question_text: For every Boolean function f:{-1,1}^n→{-1,1}, is the sum of its linear Fourier coefficients bounded by the square root of its total degree, i.e. does ∑_{i=1}^n \hat f(i) ≤ √(deg(f)) always hold?

evidence.quote: Statement: Let f : {− 1, 1}n → {− 1, 1}. Then ∑n i= 1 ˆf (i) ≤ √ deg( f ).

accepted.question_text: Fix an integer d≥1 and ε∈(0,1). What is the smallest k=k(d,ε) such that whenever p:R^n→R is a degree-d polynomial and X is an R^n-valued random vector whose coordinates are each standard Gaussian and are k-wise independent, the sign test of p under X approximates the true Gaussian one within ε, i.e. |Pr[p(X)≥0]-Pr[p(Z)≥0]|≤ε for Z∼N(0,I_n)?
accepted.context_brief: Bounded independence for polynomial threshold functions

evidence.quote: Statement: Fix d ∈ /C6 and ǫ∈ (0, 1). Determine the least k = k(d, ǫ) such that the following holds: If p : /CA n → /CA is any degree- d multivariate polynomial, and X is any /CA n-valued random variable with the property that each X i has the standard Gaussian distribution and each collection X i1, . . .,X i k is inde- pendent, then | Pr[p(X ) ≥ 0] − Pr[p(Z) ≥ 0]| ≤ ǫ, where Z has the standard n-dimensional Gaussian distribution.

accepted.question_text: For each constant δ>0, do s^{-O(1)}-biased distributions fool size-s DNF formulas to error at most δ? Equivalently, if f:{0,1}^n→{-1,1} is computable by a size-s DNF and φ is an s^{-O(1)}-biased distribution on {0,1}^n, must |E_{x uniform}[f(x)]-E_{y∼φ}[f(y)]|≤δ?
accepted.context_brief: Pseudorandomness for DNFs from small bias

evidence.quote: Statement: Is it true for each constant δ > 0 that s− O(1)-biased densities δ-fool size- s DNFs? I.e., that if f : {0, 1}n → {− 1, 1} is computable by a size- s DNF and ϕ is an s− O(1)-biased density on {0, 1}, then | Ex∼ {0,1}n[ f (x)] − Ey∼ ϕ [ f (y)]| ≤ δ.

accepted.question_text: Does every polynomial-threshold-function representation of the inner-product-mod-2 function IP_{2n}:{0,1}^{2n}→{-1,1} require at least 3^n monomials?
accepted.context_brief: PTF sparsity for inner product mod 2

evidence.quote: Statement: Is it true that any PTF representation of the inner product mod 2 function on 2 n bits, IP2n : /BY 2n 2 → {− 1, 1}, requires at least 3 n monomi- als?

accepted.question_text: Fix ε>0. Is every monotone Boolean function f:{-1,1}^n→{-1,1} ε-close to a junta whose size is polynomial in deg(f)?
accepted.context_brief: Monotone functions close to low-degree juntas

evidence.quote: Statement: Fix any ǫ > 0. Then every monotone f : {− 1, 1}n → {− 1, 1} is ǫ-close to a poly(deg( f ))-junta.
• RESOLVED (in the negative) by Daniel Kane, 2012.

accepted.question_text: If f:{-1,1}^n→{-1,1} is monotone, must its total influence I[f] be little-o of its maximum sensitivity sens[f]?

evidence.quote: Statement: Let f : {− 1, 1}n → {− 1, 1} be monotone. Then I[ f ] < o(sens[ f ]).

accepted.question_text: What is the minimum degree of a polynomial-valued function f:{-1,1}^n→[-1,-2/3]∪[2/3,1] that behaves like an approximate majority, meaning f(x)∈[2/3,1] whenever ∑_{i=1}^n x_i≥n/2 and f(x)∈[-1,-2/3] whenever ∑_{i=1}^n x_i≤-n/2?

evidence.quote: Statement: What is the least possible degree of a function f : {− 1, 1}n → [− 1, − 2/3] ∪ [2/3, 1] which has f (x) ∈ [2/3, 1] whenever ∑n i= 1 xi ≥ n/2 and has f (x) ∈ [− 1, − 2/3] whenever ∑n i= 1 xi ≤ − n/2?

accepted.question_text: Suppose q_1,…,q_m:F_2^n→F_2 are polynomials of degree at most 2 and the Boolean AND function on F_2^n can be written as AND(x)=∑_{i=1}^m c_i(-1)^{q_i(x)} for real coefficients c_i. What lower bound on m is necessary?

evidence.quote: Statement: Suppose q1, . . .,qm : /BY n 2 → /BY 2 are polynomials of degree at most 2 and suppose the indicator function of (1 , . . .,1) ∈ /BY n 2 , namely AND : /BY n 2 → {− 1, 1}, is expressible as AND( x) = ∑m i= 1 ci(− 1)qi(x) for some real numbers ci. What is a lower bound for m?
